thread_analysis.thread_summary: [COMPANY] requests a quote for a Korean-manufactured audio module (BCM-SQ800, built on a QCC3095 chip) that does not appear on the Bluetooth SIG registration site. The consultant works through what registration scope and testing would actually be required depending on whether the module has its own RF/RF PHY evidence, whether its Host Stack is an unauthenticated open-source implementation (which would be prohibitively costly to test), or whether it is a simple HCI-only module with no embedded Host stack -- in which case only RF/RF PHY testing of the module itself, referencing the underlying chip's existing QDID, would be needed.
all_questions_found: Since the module (BCM-SQ800) does not appear on the SIG registration site, is it unauthenticated, and would Including the already-registered underlying SoC alone be sufficient, or does the module still need its own RF/RF PHY evidence?
If the module is unauthenticated, can the module manufacturer obtain a BQTF-issued RF/RF PHY report?

The quote-request form lists 'Controller Subsystem' under Host Stack -- what is the actual Host Subsystem QDID/DN, and if an unauthenticated open-source stack (such as BlueZ) is used, what would that mean for testing cost and responsibility?

Are the listed supported profiles (HFP, HSP, A2DP, AVRCP) backed by the Host Stack QDID/DN's existing certified evidence, or are they unauthenticated profiles that would require new testing in this registration?

If the module turns out to be a simple HCI-only module (Core-Controller registration only, without an embedded Host stack), can registration proceed by Including just the underlying chip's QDID and testing only RF/RF PHY?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread works through how to scope testing for an unregistered audio module by first checking whether the underlying chip alone is already registered (which is not sufficient on its own -- the module itself still needs its own RF/RF PHY evidence unless it has its own registered QDID/DN) and whether the Host Stack is a certified implementation or an unauthenticated open-source one (such as BlueZ), which would make protocol-layer testing prohibitively costly and time-consuming. It also covers an alternative, much simpler scoping scenario: if the module is actually a standard HCI-only module (a Core-Controller registration without an embedded Host stack or profiles), registration can proceed by Including only the underlying chip's existing QDID and performing RF/RF PHY testing on the module itself, since Host and Profile layer testing is not applicable to a module that doesn't implement those layers.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: An unregistered module's RF/RF PHY testing requirement cannot be avoided simply by Including the underlying chip's existing registration; the module itself needs its own evidence unless it has its own registered QDID/DN. If a product's Host Stack uses an unauthenticated open-source implementation rather than a certified one, protocol-layer testing would be enormously costly and slow, and responsibility for obtaining that evidence should be directed to the module/chip manufacturer, who bears implementation responsibility for that stack, rather than the integrator. If the module turns out to be a simple HCI-only module without an embedded Host stack, the scope simplifies considerably: only RF/RF PHY testing on the module is needed, Including just the underlying chip's QDID, since Host and Profile layers are out of scope for a module that doesn't implement them.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming Including an already-registered underlying chip is sufficient without checking whether the module itself has its own RF/RF PHY evidence would understate the true testing scope. Attempting to test an unauthenticated open-source Host Stack implementation (such as BlueZ) without recognizing the scale of cost and time involved, or without directing that responsibility to the module manufacturer, risks a severely underestimated quote. Conversely, assuming full Host/Profile testing is needed when the module is actually a simple HCI-only module would lead to over-quoting unnecessary scope.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When quoting registration for an unregistered audio or combo module, first determine whether the module itself has its own RF/RF PHY evidence (the underlying chip's registration alone is not sufficient), then determine whether its Host Stack is a certified implementation or an unauthenticated open-source one (which would be prohibitively costly to test and should be directed to the module manufacturer), and finally check whether the module is actually a simple HCI-only module with no embedded Host stack -- which would substantially simplify the required scope to RF/RF PHY testing alone.
